doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Saxophones, mouthpieces and reeds
summary: She plays a P. Mauriat tenor, a Keilwerth soprano given by Michael, and discusses mouthpieces and reeds.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well I’ll lighten up a little bit. I don’t usually ask people about their gear, but I had a thing this morning I had to play tenor and I reminded myself what a lousy horn I have. Can you tell me what sax and mouthpiece you use?

Yes. On the tenor I have a P. Mauriat. I’m endorsed by the company and I met him probably 15 years ago at one of the JEN conferences and I tried them and I really really dig them right away. And I have a nice Mark VI also. But it’s a beautiful one, somebody bought it, used it for a month, put it away and sold it to me 50 years later or something like that, or 40 years later. But as I always say it’s “flarp.” It’s flarp. It’s flat and sharp. So on the palm key you have to do so much movement from one note to the other, you’re just quite never there. You know great sound but man, how much work. And a lot of times I don’t want to do a gig wondering how you’re going to land and moving so much. So that’s — and also the traveling I did a trip that they smashed my case so after that one I was approached around the same time by P. Mauriat and I thought they were great. So I started to kind of play them and to tell you the truth I’ve really never — I once in a while pull out my Mark VI just for the fun of it but I always play P. Mauriat. And the mouthpiece I’m playing a Rafael Navarro mouthpiece and I’ve been playing it for five years and I’ve really, really enjoyed them. And on the soprano I have a Keilwerth that was given to me by Michael years ago. I still have three herniated discs in my neck because of playing saxophone. So for a while I couldn’t play the tenor, I couldn’t put any weight. And I didn’t have a soprano. So you know he had probably a stack of like hundreds of saxophones and he just gave me this beautiful Keilwerth and the mouthpiece is a prototype I think a Louis — what’s the name Louis? They are Belgium. I don’t remember the name. It is metal. But you know I keep changing, I play also Selmer sometimes mouthpiece. And you know so far I am happy. But it’s always some gigs you just kind of like oh I’m going to throw away everything out you know and then the week after it’s like I love it. So I think it’s a struggle of mouthpiece, reeds, I use Vandoren reeds, ZZ, and this one has been pretty constant in my career.
They’re getting more expensive as the time goes by.
Only the gigs get paid less or stay the same.
